title: Green peas, canned, cooked with butter

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green peas cooked with butter (or margarine) are a ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh peas that are blanched, drained and packed in jars with added butter to enhance flavor and texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peas belong to the legume family and are a good source of plant protein.
Canning preserves the peas' nutrients for months without refrigeration.
Butter addition improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and K.
Peas are used worldwide in soups, stews, salads and side dishes.
Canned peas typically have a shelf life of 2 to 5 years.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned peas provides about 8–9 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas supply folate, thiamine and vitamin B6, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Good source of minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, phosphorus and potassium in peas support heart and nerve function.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Vitamin K and magnesium contribute to bone mineralization and may help prevent osteoporosis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to peas.

items.title: Added butter
items.content: The butter increases calorie density, which should be considered in weight‑management diets.

items.title: Potential BPA exposure
items.content: Metal cans can have trace BPA; avoid storing the product at high temperatures for long periods.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peas can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, soups, stews, or served as a side dish with meat. Warm gently before serving to distribute the butter evenly.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate, using within 3–4 days.
